title: prrr design map
description:
# prrr design map

Tracker: beads (`bd`). This epic is the map; its child issues are the tickets. `bd ready` is the frontier. Research findings live in `docs/research/`.

## Destination

An approved `SPEC.md` at the repo root plus an implementation plan, with every
architectural question resolved so subagents can build the package from the
plan without stalling. Nothing is implemented on the way; prototypes are
throwaway.

## Notes

- Domain: an Emacs package, `prrr`, for reviewing GitHub pull requests on top
  of magit and forge. Glossary is `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root; every session
  uses its terms.
- Standing preferences (from the human):
  - Diff render performance is critical. Large diffs must open instantly, with
    per-file folding, a Viewed flag that folds a file away, and easy jumping
    between files.
  - Every action has a mnemonic single key and a transient menu that mirrors
    it exactly (Casual-style discoverability, magit-style speed).
  - Default workflow is a server-side Pending Review with batched Submit;
    Immediate Publish is an explicit override for one comment.
  - Depend only on forge's public API (EIEIO classes, `forge-get-*`,
    `forge-pull`, status-buffer section hooks) and ghub. Never call `forge--`
    privates or extend forge's database. prrr keeps its own SQLite database.
  - The human relies heavily on PR Stacks, both as author and reviewer.
  - Agent integration is bi-directional through a public API: an agent can add
    Pending Review comments as the user (to be read and edited before Submit),
    and the user can hand a PR plus pending comments to an agent from prrr.
    No agent code ships in the package.
  - Tree-sitter syntax highlighting of the diff: decided GO (see Decisions),
    applied only when a file section is expanded.
- The project will be open-sourced. Every committed file must be publishable:
  no personal paths or tokens, GPL-3.0-or-later (the Emacs package
  convention), MELPA-ready package headers, and decisions written for an
  outside reader.
- Skills to consult when working tickets: `mattpocock-skills:grilling` and
  `mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling` for grilling tickets;
  `mattpocock-skills:prototype` for prototype tickets;
  `mattpocock-skills:research` for research tickets.
- Prior art the human has not used but suspects has sharp edges: pr-review.el,
  code-review.el. The human's own `~/.emacs.d/lisp/crit-review.el` holds
  reusable UX (region anchoring, capture buffer, next/prev, transient) and the
  agent handoff shape (JSON review file, emacsclient entry point).
- Settled before the map (recorded in `CONTEXT.md` and here, no ticket):
  Review Queue lives in the current repo's magit-status buffer only. Review
  Buffer derives from magit-diff-mode and diffs the local refs forge fetches.
  Threads render as real magit sections under the anchored line; File
  Comments at the top of their file section; outdated Threads in a folded
  section at the end of their file, and a buffer-level folded section for
  files no longer in the diff. The Review Buffer has folded header sections
  for the PR description and discussion, plus a key to forge's topic buffer.
  Non-default Ranges are read-only until research says otherwise. Team
  memberships are fetched once and cached with a refresh command. Nothing
  is merged from prrr.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per resolved ticket: [title](issues/NN-slug.md): gist -->

- [Research: GitHub API for Pending Reviews, comment anchoring, replies, and Ranges] (prrr-t9q.2): GraphQL for the whole Pending Review lifecycle (`addPullRequestReview` with no event, `addPullRequestReviewThread` with file line + side, `startLine` for ranges, `subjectType: FILE` for files, `submitPullRequestReview` with the Verdict). Threads anchor to the review's commit; a diff between two arbitrary PR commits cannot take comments, so non-default Ranges stay read-only. Immediate Publish of one Review Comment is REST-only. Limits and deprecations listed in the findings.
- [Research: GitHub API for fetching Threads, resolving them, and the Viewed flag] (prrr-t9q.3): one `reviewThreads(first:100)` query per PR costs 1 rate-limit point and returns path, line/startLine, diffSide, isOutdated, isResolved, subjectType, and comments with state PENDING|SUBMITTED. The Pending Review is read via `reviews(states:[PENDING], author:)`. `resolveReviewThread`/`unresolveReviewThread` return the thread. Viewed is `viewerViewedState` (VIEWED|UNVIEWED|DISMISSED) per (PR, path, viewer) with `markFileAsViewed`/`unmarkFileAsViewed`; GitHub resets it when the file changes, and it has no commit argument, so it fits only the default Range. "New commits since my review" = viewer's latest submitted review `commit.oid` vs `headRefOid`. Forge already stores the description (`body`) and Discussion Comments (`posts`) publicly; Threads need prrr's own store. Queries were run live; mutations transcribed from docs.
- [Research: GitHub API for queue filters, team membership, and Stack detection] (prrr-t9q.4): forge publicly stores draft-p, author, assignees, review-requests (users only; Team requests are dropped and satisfied requests vanish on the next pull), base-ref/head-ref/head-rev, cross-repo-p, state, their-id (GitHub node id). Its `reviews` slot is never filled and `teams` is always nil, so prrr must fetch Team requests, Team memberships (`viewer.organizations.teams(userLogins:)`), and review history (`latestReviews` with `onBehalfOf`, `viewerLatestReview`, `viewerLatestReviewRequest`) itself. Stack rule: same repo, both open, A.base-ref equals B.head-ref, B not cross-repo. PR heads are at `refs/pullreqs/N` via forge's refspec. Add the queue section with `magit-add-section-hook` before `forge-insert-pullreqs`; use `forge-query`/`forge-rest` for prrr's own calls; read "me" from `github.user` git config as the public path.
- [Research: tree-sitter syntax highlighting inside a magit diff buffer] (prrr-t9q.5): GO, deferred to file-section expansion. One treesit parser per file section per side with included ranges set to the line bodies (prefix char excluded), font-lock rules taken from the cached `treesit-font-lock-settings` of the language's ts-mode and applied with a small `treesit-query-capture` loop that prepends to `font-lock-face`. Measured on Emacs 31.1: 1.3 / 9.7 / 34 ms per 100 / 300 / 1,000-line section, 0 ms while collapsed, ~400 ms eager for a 10.6k-line diff. Do not use `treesit-font-lock-fontify-region` or `treesit-range-settings` (they assume a primary parser and write `face`). Keep `magit-diff-fontify-hunk` nil in prrr buffers; it is a usable fallback for languages without a grammar.
- [Prototype: lazy per-file washing with thread sections in a magit-diff-mode buffer] (prrr-t9q.1): hybrid lazy rendering approved by the human. File list first (65 ms at 417 files, 355 ms at 2516), auto-expand the top ~30 files / 2,000 lines, wash the rest on expand (2 to 7 ms per file). Threads are real child sections via a copied hunk washer; two magit internals need advice; refresh preserves folds and Viewed. Prototype kept on branch `prototype/lazy-diff`.
- [Data model and local database: what is cached, keys, and invalidation] (prrr-t9q.7): plain emacsql tables with structs, one SQLite file under user-emacs-directory, GitHub node ids as primary keys. Tables: pullreq-meta, thread, review-comment, pending-review, viewed, team, pr-bookmark, outbox, schema-version. Review Buffer renders from the database then refetches in the background; the queue renders from pullreq-meta with `prrr-pull` refreshing when older than 5 minutes; writes are optimistic with an outbox for failures; server rows win on refetch except unsent outbox rows.
- [Review Queue: Review States, ordering, and Stack display] (prrr-t9q.6): eight For Me states (new-commits first) and five Mine states; drafts hidden unless requested or assigned; FIFO ordering with an Awaiting me partition sorted by PR age (oldest first, a push re-enters at age position) and a Served partition sorted by my last touch; Stacks as indented bottom-up chains that sort together; queue line matches forge; section before forge's PR section, expanded when non-empty.
- [Ranges: selecting commits, since-last-review, and Viewed interaction] (prrr-t9q.9): five Range kinds (default, since-review, since-opened, commit, between). RIGHT side of any Range ending at head is commentable as a default-Range comment; everything else is read-only with a jump key. Threads outside the Range fold into a "not in range" section. Viewed is GitHub's flag only. Stack navigation opens the neighbour PR at its own default Range. Bookmark updates on close, Submit, or "mark as seen". Force-push: pin needed commits as refs/prrr/<n>/<oid>, tree-diff across rewrites with a notice, fetch by sha or fall back to default, and never re-render an open buffer under the user.
- [Agent extension API: bi-directional surface] (prrr-t9q.8): ten `prrr-api-*` functions over structs, callable in-process or via emacsclient, including JSON export/import in v1. Agent comments go straight to the Pending Review with the user's token by default (`prrr-agent-comment-mode`, with a `proposed` local-until-accepted alternative), flagged agent-p with a badge and a Submit confirmation. Four hooks plus `prrr-agent-invoke-function` as the only agent seam; "send to agent" renders a Markdown payload into agent-shell or the kill ring. No attribution text unless `prrr-agent-comment-prefix` is set.

## Not yet specified

- Magit coupling policy: the prototype copies `magit-diff-wash-hunk` and
  advises two internals (`magit-diff--hunk-section`, `magit-diff-hunk-line`).
  Decide whether the package pins a magit version range, vendors the washer,
  or asks upstream for a hook. Sharpens when the spec's rendering section is
  written.

- Testing strategy for the package: how to test rendering against recorded
  diffs and the API layer against recorded GitHub responses, without a live
  token. Sharpens once the data model and API surface are decided.
- Editing and deleting one's own comments, resolving and unresolving Threads,
  reactions, and GitHub "suggested changes" blocks: which of these are in v1
  and how they surface. Depends on the API research and the keymap.
- Notifications: whether prrr should tell the user about new activity on PRs
  in the Review Queue, or leave that to forge's notification support.

## Out of scope

- The keymap and transient menus prototype (prrr-t9q.10): closed unresolved at the human's request; the key table is decided directly in SPEC.md and will be adjusted during implementation review.

- GitLab and every forge other than GitHub.
- Reviewing issues or discussions; only pull requests.
- A cross-repo Review Queue (the human chose current-repo only for now).
- AI-assisted review itself; only the extension points ship.
- Contributing any of this upstream into forge.
- Merging the PR from prrr; `forge-merge` exists.
close_reason: Design map complete: SPEC.md approved, milestone 1 implemented on branch foundation

title: Make prrr.el autoload-driven so (require 'prrr) does not load forge at startup
description: prrr.el eagerly requires prrr-github, which loads forge and magit (~150 ms). When commands exist, autoload them and require prrr-github from the commands.

title: Document the Stack tie rule once forge's input order is fixed
description: Two open PRs with the same head-ref: prrr-state--parent picks the first in PRS order. Document and test once the queue builder fixes the order of PRS from forge.

title: Review Queue UI must not assume stack-size equals visible rows
description: When the viewer's own PR is dropped from a For Me stack, the remaining entries still report the full stack-size (test queue-stack-in-for-me-omits-my-own-member pins 2/2 for a one-row stack).

title: Clear prrr-db-preserved-outbox after showing it to the user
description: After a schema reset the preserved outbox rows are left in prrr-db-preserved-outbox; the consumer that displays them must clear the variable.

title: Decide which head oid new-commits compares against
description: prrr-pr-meta-head-oid is stored by prrr-pull but prrr-state uses prrr-pr-head-oid from forge's head-rev. Forge's and prrr's fetch cadences differ; pick one and document it in the prrr-pr builder.

title: Treat a null pullRequest as an error before persisting
description: prrr-github-decode-review-data on a deleted or wrong-numbered PR yields pr-id nil and an empty plist; the fetch callback must not persist it.

title: Fetch functions need an error path (errorback into Outbox)
description: prrr-github-fetch-queue, -teams and -review-data have no :errorback; a failed request hands the decoder nil or surfaces ghub's default error. Milestone 2 must route failures to the Outbox / header state per SPEC.md section 11.

title: Prototype: keymap and transient menus for the Review Buffer and Review Queue
description:
Produce the full key table and the transient menu layout for the Review
Buffer and the Review Queue section, as a throwaway prototype the human can
load and press keys in (menus can call stubs). Constraints: every action has
a mnemonic single key; the transient mirrors them exactly; no collisions with
the magit-diff-mode and magit-section keys the user still needs (TAB, n, p,
RET, g, q, j); which key opens the menu (`?` versus `C-o` versus `h`);
sub-menus for comment, review, range, stack, viewed, and agent actions. The
resolution is the key table and menu structure, recorded for the spec.
close_reason: Superseded: the human chose to skip the keymap prototype; the key table and transient layout are decided directly in SPEC.md

title: Ranges: selecting commits, since-last-review, and Viewed interaction
description:
Decide the Range model. How the user picks a Range (default merge-base to
head; a single commit; between two commits; since my last review); how
"since my last review" is computed from review history; whether commenting is
allowed on non-default Ranges per the API research, and if so how line
numbers map; how the Viewed flag behaves when the Range is not the default
(GitHub's flag is per PR, not per range); and how Stack navigation sets the
Range when moving to the PR above or below.
notes:
Resolved 2026-10-10 by grilling (two rounds).

## Range kinds

- `default`: merge-base to head. The only Range GitHub comments on directly.
- `since-review`: my latest submitted review's commit to head.
- `since-opened`: the Bookmark head (last visit in prrr) to head.
- `commit`: one PR commit against its parent.
- `between`: two chosen PR commits.
The header line always names the current Range. A Range transient lists the
kinds; `commit` and `between` pick from the PR's commits via completing-read.
Switching preserves point on the same file and line when it exists.

## Commenting per Range

- RIGHT side of any Range that ends at head (`default`, `since-review`,
  `since-opened`): commentable; line numbers are head line numbers, so these
  are ordinary default-Range comments.
- LEFT side of `since-review` / `since-opened`, and both sides of `commit` /
  `between`: read-only. A key jumps to the same file and line in the default
  Range to comment.

## Threads per Range

Threads whose anchor line is in the Range render inline. Threads on lines
not in the Range go to the per-file folded section labelled "not in range"
(distinct from "outdated").

## Viewed

GitHub's flag only (per PR and path), shown and toggled on every Range. No
local per-range Viewed.

## Stack navigation

Moving to the PR above or below opens that PR's Review Buffer at its own
default Range in the same window. Each PR diffs against its own base; no
whole-Stack diff.

## Bookmark

Updated on Review Buffer close and on Submit, not on open, so `since-opened`
means "since my previous visit". A manual "mark as seen" command also
updates it.

## Force-push and moving heads

1. prrr pins every commit it may need later as a local ref
   `refs/prrr/<pr-number>/<oid>` when it records a Bookmark, learns a review
   commit, or submits, so forge's refspec update and git gc cannot drop them.
2. If the Range's start commit is not an ancestor of head, diff the two trees
   directly (`git diff OLD HEAD`) and show a "history rewritten" notice in
   the header.
3. If the start commit is not available locally, fetch it by sha from the
   remote; if that fails, fall back to `default` with a message.
4. While a Review Buffer is open and a background refetch sees the head oid
   change, the header shows "head moved, press g"; nothing re-renders
   underneath the user. Pending Review comments remain (GitHub keeps them and
   marks them outdated).
close_reason: Resolved; Range kinds, commenting rules, force-push handling in notes

title: Agent extension API: bi-directional surface
description:
Decide the public API that lets an agent work with a review and lets the
user hand a review to an agent. Inputs: crit-review.el's handoff
(`crit-review-start` via emacsclient, JSON file with comments and anchors,
`crit-review-reply`) and the human's preferences in the map Notes. Decide:
the Elisp functions and their data shapes (list Threads for a PR, read the
Pending Review, add a pending comment on a line/range/file as the user, reply,
read the diff for a Range); how agent-authored pending comments are marked
so the user can review and edit them before Submit; the hooks fired on
comment create, reply, submit; the command that invokes an agent with the PR
and pending comments (agent-shell first, but generic); and whether a JSON
serialization ships in v1 or is deferred. Keep agent code out of the package.
notes:
Resolved 2026-10-10 by grilling (one round).

## Surface

A documented Elisp API, one public function per operation, taking and
returning plain structs (cl-defstruct) or alists, never buffers or sections.
Every function takes a PR identifier (repository + number) so an external
process can call it through `emacsclient -e` without buffer context. In-
process agents (agent-shell tool calls) use the same functions.

Functions: `prrr-api-pullreq` (summary with Range, head, Review State),
`prrr-api-threads` (Threads with comments, optional Range filter),
`prrr-api-diff` (unified diff for a Range, or one file), `prrr-api-pending`
(the Pending Review and its comments), `prrr-api-add-comment` (line, range,
or file; flagged agent-p), `prrr-api-reply`,
`prrr-api-delete-pending-comment`, `prrr-api-submit` (Verdict and body),
`prrr-api-export` (payload as JSON file; crit-review's handoff shape extended
with GitHub ids), `prrr-api-import` (read a file of comments).

## Agent-authored comments

Default: published straight to the Pending Review on GitHub with the user's
token, flagged `agent-p` locally, rendered with a distinct face and an
"agent" badge, editable and deletable like any pending comment. Submit shows
the count of agent comments and asks for confirmation.
Configurable via `prrr-agent-comment-mode`: `pending` (default, as above) or
`proposed` (kept local with `local-state` = `proposed` until the user accepts
each one; accepted comments go to the Pending Review, rejected ones are
deleted). `review-comment.local-state` therefore gains the value `proposed`.

## Hooks and seam

`prrr-comment-created-hook`, `prrr-reply-created-hook`,
`prrr-review-submitted-hook`, `prrr-review-buffer-opened-hook`, each called
with the relevant struct. `prrr-agent-invoke-function`: the single
agent-specific seam, called by the "send to agent" command with the context
payload.

## Send to agent

A Review Buffer command builds a payload (PR summary, current Range, diff,
Threads, Pending Review including agent comments, and the user's
instructions from a compose buffer) and calls `prrr-agent-invoke-function`.
The default implementation renders the payload as Markdown and, if
agent-shell is present, submits it using crit-review's queue-or-insert
method; otherwise it copies the Markdown to the kill ring. The Markdown form
is the paste-anywhere serialization; JSON export is the file form.

## Attribution

Everything goes out under the user's account. No attribution text by
default; `prrr-agent-comment-prefix` (default empty) can prepend a marker to
agent-authored comment bodies.
close_reason: Resolved; API functions, agent comment mode, hooks, send-to-agent in notes

title: Data model and local database: what is cached, keys, and invalidation
description:
Design prrr's own SQLite schema (via emacsql, alongside forge's database)
and its freshness rules. Decide which entities are stored (Threads and
Review Comments, Pending Review, Viewed flags, Teams, per-PR Review State
inputs, Range bookmarks such as "last reviewed head"), their keys, how they
relate to forge's PR ids, what is fetched on Review Buffer open versus on the
explicit invalidate-and-refetch chord, and how writes (new comment, reply,
viewed) update the database before or after the server confirms. Decide what
the queue reads from the database so it renders with no network. Decide the
local retry queue for failed publishes. The resolution is the schema and the
freshness rules, written so the spec can include them.
notes:
Resolved 2026-10-10 by grilling; all eight recommendations accepted.

## Storage

- Plain emacsql tables with `cl-defstruct` rows. No closql.
- One SQLite file for all repositories: `prrr-database-file`, default
  `prrr-database.sqlite` under `user-emacs-directory` (forge's convention).
- Primary keys are GitHub node ids everywhere. Forge's repository id and the
  PR number are secondary columns used only to join to forge objects.
- `schema-version` row; on mismatch before 1.0, drop and recreate all tables
  except `outbox`, whose rows are surfaced to the user before any drop.

## Tables

- `pullreq-meta` (pr-id PK, forge-repo-id, number, head-oid, review-requests
  [list of (kind login-or-slug)], latest-reviews [list of (login state
  commit-oid on-behalf-of)], viewer-latest-review (state commit-oid),
  viewer-latest-review-request, fetched-at). Everything the Review Queue
  needs, so it renders with no network.
- `thread` (thread-id PK, pr-id, path, line, start-line, side, start-side,
  subject-type, outdated-p, resolved-p, original-line, original-commit,
  fetched-at).
- `review-comment` (comment-id PK, thread-id, pr-id, author, body,
  created-at, updated-at, reply-to, review-id, state [PENDING|SUBMITTED],
  local-state [sent|unsent], agent-p). `agent-p` marks comments added through
  the agent API so the user can review them before Submit.
- `pending-review` (pr-id PK, review-id, commit-oid, body, created-at).
- `viewed` (pr-id, path, state [VIEWED|UNVIEWED|DISMISSED], fetched-at;
  PK pr-id+path). Default Range only; other Ranges are ticket prrr-t9q.9.
- `team` (combined-slug PK, org, slug, fetched-at).
- `pr-bookmark` (pr-id PK, last-opened-head-oid, last-opened-at). Local
  "new since I last looked", independent of GitHub's review commit.
- `outbox` (id PK, pr-id, kind, payload, created-at, attempts, last-error).

## Freshness rules

- Review Buffer open: render from the database immediately, then refetch
  Threads, Pending Review, and Viewed in the background (stale-while-
  revalidate) with a "refreshing" indicator, and re-render when they
  arrive. The invalidate-and-refetch chord forces that refetch.
- Review Queue: renders only from `pullreq-meta` and forge's own PR data.
  `prrr-pull` fetches the per-PR queue inputs for the current repository in
  one GraphQL query; the section triggers it in the background when the
  newest `fetched-at` is older than `prrr-queue-stale-after` (default 5 min).
  No advice on `forge-pull`.
- Teams: fetched on first use, refreshed by `prrr-refresh-teams`, and
  re-fetched automatically when older than a day.
- Writes are optimistic: a new comment, reply, or Viewed toggle writes a row
  marked unsent, renders at once with a distinct face, then calls the server;
  success replaces the row with the server's node id; failure keeps it in
  `outbox` with the error, retried on the next write or refetch, with
  commands to retry or discard.
- Reconciliation on refetch: server rows replace local rows for every
  SUBMITTED comment, Thread, and Viewed flag. For the Pending Review the
  server is authoritative for comments it has accepted; unsent `outbox`
  rows survive and are re-attempted against the current pending review id.
  Comments the user added from the web appear after refetch like any other.
close_reason: Resolved; schema and freshness rules in notes

title: Review Queue: Review States, ordering, and Stack display
description:
Define the Review Queue precisely. Decide the full Review State enum per PR
(awaiting my review; awaiting my team, teammate reviewed; I approved; I
requested changes; I commented; new commits since my review) and how each
shows in the queue line. Decide ordering within each Queue Group, whether a
PR can appear in both groups, how a Stack is displayed in the queue (indented
chain, bottom first?), and what information the queue line carries (number,
title, author, state, counts of unresolved Threads, stack position). Decide
the refresh model: when the queue recomputes, and whether it needs the
database. Record the resolved vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`.
notes:
Resolved 2026-10-10 by grilling (two rounds).

## Review State (per PR, viewer's standpoint; first match wins)

For Me group: `new-commits` (I reviewed, head moved since), `requested`
(review requested from me directly), `team-requested` (requested from one of
my Teams, no team member has reviewed), `teammate-reviewed` (team request
satisfied by someone else), `changes-requested`, `approved`, `commented` (my
latest review), `assigned` (assigned, no request, no review of mine).

Mine group (author's standpoint): `draft`, `awaiting-review` (no reviews yet),
`changes-requested`, `approved`, `reviewed` (comments only), each with the
count of unresolved Threads.

## Membership

For Me: open, authored by someone else, and at least one of requested,
team-requested, teammate-reviewed, assigned, or ever reviewed by me. Drafts
are excluded unless directly requested from me or assigned to me; such drafts
show dimmed with their state and do not enter Awaiting me until marked ready
for review.

Mine: open PRs I authored, drafts included.

A PR can appear in both groups only if I authored it and requested a review
from myself; show it in Mine only.

## Ordering (FIFO; optimizing time to first review and time to close)

For Me has two partitions, Awaiting me first, then Served.
- Awaiting me: states new-commits, requested, team-requested, and assigned
  with no review of mine. Sorted by PR creation time, oldest first. An
  author's push moves a Served PR back into Awaiting me at its age-determined
  position (never to the back).
- Served: I reviewed or commented and nothing was pushed since, or a
  teammate reviewed. Sorted by my last touch, oldest first.
- My comment, review, or Immediate Publish counts as a touch and moves the
  PR to Served.

Mine: creation time, oldest first, with sub-sort changes-requested before
awaiting-review before approved before reviewed before draft.

Stacks: rendered bottom-up as an indented chain under the bottom PR with a
position marker (`⟰ 2/4`). A Stack appears in a group if any member
qualifies; non-qualifying members are shown dimmed so the chain is
navigable. A Stack sorts by its highest-ranked member (oldest Awaiting member
in For Me) and the chain stays together.

## Queue line

`#number  state-badge  title  author  stack-marker  unresolved-count
updated-ago`, faces per state, title truncated to window width, styled to
match forge's topic lines.

## Actions on a queue line (keys decided in prrr-t9q.10)

Open Review Buffer at the default Range (RET); open forge topic buffer;
browse on GitHub; checkout the PR branch (forge's command); jump through the
Stack; refresh queue (`prrr-pull`); transient toggles to show or hide drafts
and Served PRs; the main prrr transient.

## Section placement and refresh

Inserted into `magit-status-sections-hook` before forge's pull request
section via `magit-add-section-hook`. Expanded by default when non-empty;
collapsed group headers with counts only when both groups are empty.
Renders from `pullreq-meta` and forge's PR objects only; triggers `prrr-pull`
in the background when stale (see prrr-t9q.7).

## Glossary additions

Awaiting me, Served (partitions of For Me); touch (my comment, review, or
Immediate Publish on a PR).
close_reason: Resolved; states, membership, FIFO ordering, stack display in notes

title: Research: tree-sitter syntax highlighting inside a magit diff buffer
description:
Can hunks in a magit-diff-mode derived buffer be syntax-highlighted with
Emacs's built-in `treesit` on Emacs 31, per hunk or per file, at a cost that
keeps a large diff opening instantly?

Investigate primary sources: the Emacs 31 `treesit` manual (parsers on a
buffer region, `treesit-parser-set-included-ranges`, multiple parsers per
buffer, `treesit-font-lock-settings` reuse), and existing packages that
highlight diffs (`magit-delta`, `diff-hl`, `diffview`, Doom's
`magit-diff` highlighting, `treesit` based attempts if any). Determine: whether
a parser can be scoped to one hunk's added and removed lines, whether the
language's font-lock rules can be applied to that region without turning on
the major mode, what it costs, and whether it must be deferred until a file is
expanded. Report the most promising approach and a go / no-go recommendation
with the measured or documented cost.
notes:
**Go.** On Emacs 31 a hunk's added or removed lines can be parsed in place:
create one `treesit` parser per file section and side
(`treesit-parser-create LANG nil t TAG`) and set its included ranges to the
line bodies (prefix char excluded, newline included) of the context+`+` lines
(new side) or context+`-` lines (old side); tree-sitter treats the ranges as
one continuum, so the parser sees the file fragment and reports buffer
positions. The language's font-lock rules are obtained without enabling the
mode in the diff buffer by running its `*-ts-mode` once in an empty temp
buffer and caching the compiled `treesit-font-lock-settings` (~4 ms warm);
apply them with a small `treesit-query-capture` loop that prepends faces onto
`font-lock-face` (Magit's property; a direct `face` would hide the diff line
face). Do not use `treesit-font-lock-fontify-region` or
`treesit-range-settings`: both require a primary/host parser a diff buffer
does not have (measured: they signal `treesit-parser-p nil`).

Cost (C grammar, measured): parse+fontify 1.3 ms / 9.7 ms / 34 ms for
100 / 300 / 1,000-line file sections, 0 ms while collapsed, 0.1-1.6 ms to
fontify one hunk after its section is parsed. Eager whole-diff highlighting of
a 10k-line diff is ~400 ms, so it must be deferred until the file section is
expanded (and, for huge sections, to the hunk at point or an idle timer).

Also found: Magit 4.6.0+ has `magit-diff-fontify-hunk` (default nil,
"experimental ... synchronous"), which fontifies via a full blob buffer in the
file's major mode: ~234 ms before the first hunk of a 24k-line file. Usable as
a fallback for languages without a grammar; prrr should keep it nil otherwise.
No existing Emacs package highlights diffs with `treesit`.

Findings: [docs/research/treesit-diff-highlighting.md](../../../docs/research/treesit-diff-highlighting.md)

title: Research: GitHub API for queue filters, team membership, and Stack detection
description:
From GitHub's GraphQL documentation and forge's public API (read the forge
sources in `~/.emacs.d/var/elpa/forge-*/`, public symbols only), establish:

1. Which of the queue inputs forge already stores on `forge-pullreq` and
   `forge-repository` (draft-p, review-requests including Team requests,
   assignees, author, base-ref, head-ref, head-rev, reviews) and how each is
   read with public accessors. Note whether forge's `review-requests` keeps a
   requested Team or only users, and whether it keeps requests that GitHub
   has already satisfied.
2. The GraphQL query to list the viewer's Teams across organizations, and how
   a team review request is represented on a PR (`requestedReviewer` union).
3. How to detect that a teammate reviewed in the user's place (a Team request
   satisfied by another member) when the request itself has been removed.
4. Stack detection from forge data: a PR whose `base-ref` equals another open
   PR's `head-ref` in the same repository. Confirm forge exposes both for
   cross-repo (fork) PRs too and what the fields hold.
5. Whether forge exposes a public hook or section function to add a custom
   section to magit-status (`forge-insert-*` functions and
   `magit-status-sections-hook` conventions), and what `forge-pull` fetches
   (`refs/pull/*/head` refspec) so the spec can state the local-ref assumption.

Deliver as a findings file so the spec can cite the queries and accessors.
notes:
Findings: [docs/research/queue-filters-api.md](../../../docs/research/queue-filters-api.md)
(forge 20260926.1226, GitHub GraphQL schema fetched 2026-10-10; every claim
cites file:line or URL).

1. forge stores `draft-p`, `author`, `assignees`, `review-requests`,
   `base-ref`/`base-rev`/`base-repo`, `head-ref`/`head-rev`/`head-repo`/
   `head-user`, `cross-repo-p`, `state`, `their-id` on `forge-pullreq`; read
   with `oref`. `assignees`/`review-requests` are lists of
   `(ID LOGIN NAME FORGE-ID)`. forge's query selects only `... on User { id }`
   for `requestedReviewer`, so Team requests are dropped; the slot mirrors
   GitHub's current `reviewRequests` at pull time, so satisfied requests are
   gone. The `reviews` slot is never filled (reading it signals). The
   `forge-repository` `teams` slot is always nil in this version.
2. Teams: `viewer { organizations { nodes { login teams(userLogins:[$me]) {
   nodes { slug combinedSlug } } } } }`; on a PR `requestedReviewer` is
   `Bot | EnterpriseTeam | Mannequin | Team | User`.
3. Teammate-in-my-place: `latestReviews { author { login } onBehalfOf { slug } }`
   against my Team list, and/or `timelineItems(itemTypes:
   [REVIEW_REQUESTED_EVENT, REVIEW_REQUEST_REMOVED_EVENT, PULL_REQUEST_REVIEW])`
   with `requestedReviewer { ... on Team { combinedSlug } }`.
4. Stack: same `repository`, both `open`, `(oref A base-ref)` non-nil and
   `equal` to `(oref B head-ref)`, and `(oref B cross-repo-p)` nil. Bottom
   PR: `base-ref` equals `(oref repo default-branch)`.
5. forge adds `forge-insert-pullreqs` etc. to `magit-status-sections-hook`
   via `magit-add-section-hook`; third parties do the same (public
   `forge-insert-topics` needs the private `forge--topics-spec`, so prrr
   should write its own inserter over `(oref repo pullreqs)`). Refspec:
   `+refs/pull/*/head:refs/pullreqs/*` added by `forge-add-repository` /
   `forge-add-pullreq-refspec`; `forge-pull` pulls API data then runs
   `git fetch <remote>`, so PR N's head is at `refs/pullreqs/N`.

title: Research: GitHub API for fetching Threads, resolving them, and the Viewed flag
description:
From GitHub's GraphQL documentation (primary sources only), establish how prrr
fetches and mutates review state per PR:

1. The `reviewThreads` query: every field prrr needs (path, line, startLine,
   diffSide, isOutdated, isResolved, originalLine, originalCommit,
   subjectType, comments with author/body/createdAt/replyTo/pullRequestReview
   state), pagination, and the cost in GraphQL rate-limit points for a PR with
   hundreds of comments.
2. Fetching the viewer's own Pending Review and its comments in the same or a
   separate query.
3. `resolveReviewThread` / `unresolveReviewThread`.
4. The Viewed flag: `viewerViewedState` on `PullRequest.files`,
   `markFileAsViewed` / `unmarkFileAsViewed`, and when GitHub resets the flag.
5. `reviews` and `latestReviews` / `latestOpinionatedReviews`,
   `reviewDecision`, and timeline events needed to compute "new commits since
   my review".
6. Fetching the PR's Discussion Comments and description (or confirming forge
   already stores these publicly: check `forge-pullreq` slots `body` and
   `posts`).

Deliver as a findings file with queries that can be pasted into GitHub's
explorer, so the spec can cite them.
notes:
Findings, with paste-ready queries and per-claim citations:
[docs/research/threads-viewed-api.md](../../../docs/research/threads-viewed-api.md).

1. Threads come from `PullRequest.reviewThreads(first: 100)` with nested
   `comments(first: 100)`; the thread carries `path`, `line`, `startLine`,
   `diffSide`, `startDiffSide`, `originalLine`, `isOutdated`, `isResolved`,
   `subjectType` (`LINE`/`FILE`), `viewerCanResolve`; each comment carries
   `author`, `body`, `createdAt`, `state` (`PENDING`/`SUBMITTED`), `replyTo`,
   `commit`, `originalCommit`, `pullRequestReview { state }`. Comments have
   no side field. One page of 100 threads x 100 comments costs 1 point
   (1 + 100 requests, /100, rounded), 10,100 nodes; a PR with hundreds of
   comments is 1-3 points of the 5,000/hour budget. Over-long threads are
   paged via `node(id:) { ... on PullRequestReviewThread { comments } }`.
2. The Pending Review is `reviews(states: [PENDING], author: $login)` with
   its `comments`; `latestReviews` excludes pending by definition. Whether
   pending comments also appear in `reviewThreads` is unverified.
3. `resolveReviewThread` / `unresolveReviewThread` take `threadId` and
   return the updated `thread`; gate on `viewerCanResolve` /
   `viewerCanUnresolve` (author or write access).
4. Viewed: `files { path changeType viewerViewedState }` with
   `VIEWED` / `UNVIEWED` / `DISMISSED` ("new changes since last viewed");
   `markFileAsViewed` / `unmarkFileAsViewed` take `pullRequestId` + `path`.
   GitHub unmarks a file "if the file changes after you view the file"; the
   flag is per (PR, path, viewer) with no commit argument, so it only fits
   the default Range. Finer reset rules are unverified.
5. "New commits since my review": compare the viewer's latest submitted
   review's `commit.oid` with `headRefOid`; list changes with
   `timelineItems(itemTypes: [PULL_REQUEST_COMMIT, HEAD_REF_FORCE_PUSHED_EVENT,
   PULL_REQUEST_REVIEW, REVIEW_REQUESTED_EVENT, REVIEW_DISMISSED_EVENT])`.
   `reviewDecision` is `APPROVED` / `CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `REVIEW_REQUIRED`
   or null. `latestOpinionatedReviews` behaved inconsistently live.
6. forge stores the description in `forge-pullreq` slot `body` and the
   Discussion Comments as `forge-pullreq-post` objects in slot `posts`
   (`author`, `created`, `updated`, `body`); `forge-pullreq-post` has no
   path/line/side/review slots, so Threads need prrr's own store. The
   GitHub node ID for mutations must be fetched (`pullRequest { id }`);
   forge's `id` is its own composite key.

title: Research: GitHub API for Pending Reviews, comment anchoring, replies, and Ranges
description:
From GitHub's GraphQL and REST documentation (primary sources only), establish
exactly how prrr must call the API for the review-comment lifecycle:

1. Creating a Pending Review (`addPullRequestReview` with no event, or the
   REST equivalent), discovering an existing pending review for the viewer,
   and what happens if two exist.
2. Adding a Thread to a Pending Review on a single line, a multi-line range
   (`startLine`/`line`, `startSide`/`side`), and a whole file
   (`subjectType: FILE`), including what line numbers mean (file line at the
   commit, not diff position) and which side (LEFT/RIGHT) means what.
3. Replying to an existing Thread, both inside a Pending Review and as an
   Immediate Publish.
4. Immediate Publish of one comment, and of a Discussion Comment.
5. Submitting a Pending Review with each Verdict, editing and deleting pending
   comments before Submit, and discarding a Pending Review.
6. Commenting against a non-default Range: what `commitId` / `commit_id`
   means, whether comments may anchor to an intermediate commit of the PR
   branch, and whether a diff between two arbitrary PR commits can take
   comments at all.
7. Rate limits, pagination limits, and any known pitfalls (for example, the
   REST `position` field being deprecated).

Deliver as a findings file with the exact mutation or endpoint, required
fields, and a short note per item, so the spec can cite it.
notes:
Findings: [docs/research/review-comment-api.md](../../../docs/research/review-comment-api.md).

Use GraphQL for the Pending Review lifecycle; current mutations address
lines by file line number at the commit plus a `side` (LEFT = deleted line,
old file number; RIGHT = added or context line, new file number), never by
diff position (deprecated in both APIs).

1. Create: `addPullRequestReview {pullRequestId}` with no `event` (REST:
   `POST .../pulls/{n}/reviews` with blank `event`). Discover with
   `pullRequest.reviews(states: [PENDING], author: <login>)`. No doc states
   the one-pending-review rule or the error on a second create: unverified;
   query first, treat a create error as "already exists".
2. Thread: `addPullRequestReviewThread {pullRequestReviewId, path, body,
   line, side}`; range adds `startLine, startSide` (`line`/`side` are the
   end); file comment uses `subjectType: FILE` with no line. No commit field:
   every thread anchors to the review's commit. Batch form
   `addPullRequestReview.threads` is line-only (no `subjectType`).
3. Reply: `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply {pullRequestReviewThreadId, body,
   pullRequestReviewId}`; omit the review id to publish now (unverified in
   docs). REST documented path: `POST .../pulls/{n}/comments/{id}/replies`
   (top-level comment id only, replies to replies unsupported).
4. Immediate Publish of one Review Comment: REST `POST .../pulls/{n}/
   comments {body, commit_id, path, line, side[, start_line, start_side,
   subject_type]}` is the only documented path; GraphQL equivalents are
   unverified. Discussion Comment: `addComment {subjectId, body}` or
   `POST .../issues/{n}/comments`.
5. Submit: `submitPullRequestReview {pullRequestReviewId, event, body}` with
   `APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT` (REST `POST .../reviews/{id}/
   events`). Edit/delete pending comments with
   `updatePullRequestReviewComment` / `deletePullRequestReviewComment`;
   discard with `deletePullRequestReview` (REST `DELETE .../reviews/{id}`,
   pending only).
6. `commitId` is the commit the comment applies to; GitHub remaps to head
   (`line`, `commit`) and keeps `originalLine`, `originalCommit`,
   `isOutdated`. The docs allow any SHA, so anchoring to an intermediate PR
   commit is permitted by contract (only via create-review `commitOID` or
   REST `commit_id`; unverified beyond the docs' wording). A diff between two
   arbitrary PR commits cannot take comments: there is no base-commit field,
   and LEFT always means the PR base. Non-default Ranges stay read-only;
   at most RIGHT-side/file comments via REST Immediate Publish could be
   allowed later.
7. 5,000 points/hour primary; secondary: 100 concurrent, 2,000 GraphQL
   points/min (mutation = 5), 80 content-creating requests/min and 500/hour,
   wait 1 s between mutations. `first`/`last` required and capped at 100;
   REST `per_page` max 100. Use `fullDatabaseId` when mixing with REST.

title: Prototype: lazy per-file washing with thread sections in a magit-diff-mode buffer
description:
Can a buffer derived from `magit-diff-mode` open a large diff (target: 300+
files, 20k+ changed lines, measured on a real repo) in well under a second by
rendering only the file list first and washing each file's hunks on first
expand, while still inserting Thread sections under specific lines inside
hunks, with TAB folding, `n`/`p` navigation, `magit-section` jump-to-file, and
`RET` to visit the file all working?

Build a throwaway prototype that: diffs two local refs; inserts one section
per file from `git diff --stat` output, collapsed; on expand runs
`git diff <range> -- <file>` and washes it with a copy of magit's hunk washer
modified to insert a fake Thread section after chosen line numbers; folds a
file away when marked Viewed. Record open time, expand time per file, and
whether magit's refresh (`g`) preserves fold state. Note anything in
`magit-section` that fights the design, and whether washing all files up front
is fast enough that laziness is unnecessary.

Resolution is a decision: which rendering strategy the spec commits to, with
numbers.
notes:
Resolved 2026-10-10 by the human trying the prototype: "looks great and the
performance is acceptable as a baseline".

Decision: the Review Buffer derives from `magit-diff-mode` and renders
**hybrid lazy**. On open it inserts one collapsed section per changed file
from `git diff --numstat`, then auto-expands from the top until a budget of
about 30 files or 2,000 changed lines (about 100 ms); every other file is
washed on first expand. Threads and File Comments are real child sections
(types `thread` and `file-comment`) inserted by a copy of magit's hunk washer.
Eager washing of everything is ruled out above a few hundred files.

Measured (Emacs 31.1, rails, 118 / 417 / 861 / 2516 files): open with file
list only 31 / 65 / 113 / 355 ms; expand one file 2 to 7 ms (117 to 134 ms for
a 20k-line file); expand-all 269 ms / 1.3 s / 4.4 s / 46 s; refresh with 3
files expanded 25 / 179 / 691 / 3500 ms. Stock `magit-diff-range` on the same
ranges: 213 ms / 7.0 s (417 / 2516). Refresh preserves expanded files, folded
Threads, and Viewed at every size. `RET` visits the blob at the correct line
on refs, including lines after a Thread.

Constraints the spec must carry (from "What fought the design"):
- Deferred section bodies use `magit-insert-section-body`; `magit-git-wash`
  cannot run inside one (its cancel throws to a missing catch), so use
  `magit-git-insert` plus narrowing.
- magit's hunk painting (`magit-section-paint`) and line mapping
  (`magit-diff-hunk-line`) assume hunks have no children: needs a mode-scoped
  `&context` method and one `:around` advice. `magit-diff--hunk-section`
  (internal) takes a file's first child as its first hunk: advised so a
  File Comment can come first.
- Visibility across refresh rides on `magit-section-visibility-cache`;
  restrict `magit-section-cache-visibility` to the file and thread types.
  Viewed lives in prrr's own state, not the visibility cache.
- Resolve the Range's merge base once and diff `BASE..HEAD -- FILE` per file
  (`A...B` per file recomputes the merge base, 45% of expand-all).
- Use `magit-section-inhibit-markers` `'delay` for the file list.

Primary source: branch `prototype/lazy-diff` (throwaway), files
`prototype/prrr-proto-lazy-diff.el`, `prototype/bench.el`,
`prototype/run.sh`, `prototype/RESULTS.md`. Run with `prototype/run.sh`.
